1
Introduction

1.
The Department of Prohibition, Excise and Registration (“The Department”) invites bids from
experienced agencies,who are in the field of Housekeeping, cleaning and up keeping works etc. for
three group centres of the Department.

2. All proposals submitted in response to the RFP document must be accompanied by an EMD of Rs

2,00,000 (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) in the form of Bank Guarantee in favour of Excise Commissioner
Cum I.G. Registration, Account Number – 922020004238912, Branch Name – AXIS Bank Limited Raja
Bazar, payable at Patna. Bids submitted without adequate EMD will be liable for rejection.

3. The bidders are expected to examine all instructions, forms, terms, Project requirements and other

information in the RFP documents. Failure to furnish all information required as mentioned in the
RFP documents or submission of a proposal not substantially responsive to the RFP documents in
every respect will be at the Bidder's risk and may result in rejection of the proposal.

3 Scope ofwork

1. The bidder shall provide up keeping, cleaning and housekeeping services at three Group Centres of the

Department, located at Patna, Muzaffarpur, and Bhagalpur.

2. The contract will initially be for aperiod of 2 years which may be further extended upon the satisfactory

performance of the bidder.

3. The bidder shall provide approximately 20 staffs in 2 shifts at each Group Centre. Each shift will be for 8

hours.Shifts will be as under:

4. Dress code and Identity card is mandatory for all personnel deployed.

5. The bidder shall provide well-trainedstaffs and must comply to the semi-skilled category.

6. The bidder shall maintain punctuality of workers so as to ensure timely completion of housekeeping job

daily and shall be responsible for maintaining cleanliness in all the office premises mentioned in the

Tender Document.

7. The bidder shall provide all necessary consumables,equipment to perform housekeeping work in the

premises of the Group Centres.

8. Minimum age of staff employed for the work should be 18 years and above.

9. The Agency will be responsible for compliance of all statutory provisions relating to Minimum Wages,

GST, Provident Fund, Maternity Leave Benefit and Employees State Insurance etc., if applicable in

respect of the persons deployed at the Department.

10. The persons deployed shall work as per the timings of the Group Centres in which they are deployed.

The persons deployed may be required to attend the office on Holidays or attend office before/ after

office working hours based on the exigencies of work for which no additional payment shall be made.

11. The Agency shall depute a coordinator who would be responsible for immediate interaction with the

Department so that optimal services of the persons deployed by the Agency could be availed without

any disruption.

12. The Agency shall immediately provide a substitute in the event of any person absenting from duty on

any day, leaving the job or is removed within 3 working days otherwise the penalty shall be levied.

13. . The Agency shall furnish the following documents in respect of the individual Manpower who will be

deployed at the Department before the commencement of work.

a. List of persons deployed

b. Biodata of the person

c. Attested copy of the Certificates and documents showing age, educational qualifications, and

experience

d. Character certificate from two Group “A”/ Class-I officers of the Central/State Government.

e. Certificate of verification of antecedents of persons by local Police authority.

f. Identity Cards bearing photograph

g. Aadhar number of the persons deployed (copy of the Aadhar Card maybe provided).

14. The transportation, food, medical and other statutory obligations requirements in respect of each

personnel shall be borne by the bidder.

15. The place of jurisdiction shall be Patna, Bihar for handing any disputes arising out of this

contract/agreement.

16. The bidder shall be entirely responsible for redressing grievances or resolution of disputes relating to

the personnel deployed.

17. The bidder shall ensure that all the personnel deployed by it gets minimum wages and all other

benefits admissible under Labour laws Act and shall be responsible for fulfilling obligations towards

such personnel deployed under law in force.

18. The bidder shall also arrange to get registered the mobile number of all personnel deployed in the

Bihar State Labour Welfare Society with their EPFO ESIC Accounts so that deployed employee persons

can be sure about the deposit of their statutory deductions in their respective accounts.

19. The bidder shall not indulge in arbitrary and adhoc transfer or shifting of any of its employees from

20. The bidder shall ensure uninterrupted services on all days as per the shift timings but in accordance

with the labour laws.

21. It shall be the responsibility of the bidders that antecedents of staffs are verified from local police

authority.

22. All liabilities arising out of accident or death while on duty shall be borne by the bidder only.

23. Any damage or loss caused by bidder’s persons to the Department in whatever shape, would be

recovered from the bidder.

24. In case the personnel deployed by agency commits any misconduct or any disciplinary action, the

agency shall be liable to take immediate action against such personnel on the report of the authorized

officers of the Department in this respect.

25. The Department can terminate the contract by giving one month notice without assigning any reason

thereof. During the notice period for termination of contract, the bidder shall keep on discharging their

duties till the expiry of notice period. It is the duty of the bidder to remove all the hardware and

text:
B. Routine Cleaning:-

a) The bidder is required to provide high quality cleaning service.

b) The bidder shall undertake all tasks normally associated with routine office cleaning to ensure that

the offices, toilets, meeting areas, public areas,furniture and floor spaces are maintained to a high

level of general cleanliness and remain presentable and fit for their intended purpose.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > B. Routine Cleaning:-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

section_path: C. Dusting/Polishing of all furniture, sills: -
text:
C. Dusting/Polishing of all furniture, sills: -

a) All chairs and soft furnishings must be clean, dry and free from dust.

b) All telephones should be free from dust and smears.

c) Light fittings must be free from dust.

d) All blinds and curtains should be free of strains, marks and dust.

e) All signage, including emergency signage should be clean, dry and free of strains,marks and dust.

f) Bins must be empty,clean and dry inside and out,bin-liners replaced where necessary and placed

in their original locations.Liners should be used in all containers.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > C. Dusting/Polishing of all furniture, sills: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
D. Polishing /vacuum cleaning/cleaning of floors: -


All hard floor surfaces must be free from debris, clean, dry and free of stain marks and dust. There
must be no evidence of any accumulation of slurry of soaps or residues of other cleaning agents.
Floors must be safe and not slippery. The dressing must be complete and intact without evidence of
powdering, discoloration or build up. Chewing gum and other sticky substances shall be removed
before any cleaning procedure is carried out using an appropriate cleaning technique and chewing
gum remover. Special care shall be utilized to ensure that all methods formulated agents and tools
are not injurious to the surfaces being cleaned and redressed.


All carpets, carpet tiles, mats and mat wells must be free from grit, dust and debris with no apparent
stains. They must be clean and dry; all carpeted areas are to be cleaned by the manufactures
recommended methods and recommended intervals.


The pile in the main traffic areas must be evenly brushed and opened against the flow of incoming
traffic.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > D. Polishing /vacuum cleaning/cleaning of floors: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:

Care is to be exercised when staff is still on the premises. Wet floors should be sign-posted. Trailing
cables and open sockets should be made safe.


All cleaning methods used must be of a sufficient quality to meet these standards and to maintain
any guarantees on the floor covering.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > D. Polishing /vacuum cleaning/cleaning of floors: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
E. Cleaning of all toilets :-


The required service standard is to be evident before start of activities at the Group centre and in
addition should be brought up to this standard during the operating hours. Toilets must be cleaned
thrice a day.


All furniture and fittings must be free from debris, stains marks and dust. They must be clean and dry
with no evidence of residual cleaning agents. All sanitaryware including showers, shower heads sinks,
wash hand basins. WC bowls, seat cover, hinges, tops, undersides, rims, taps, overflows, outlets,
chains, plugs, urinal, brushes, toilet roll holders, tiled surfaces, splash backs and vanity units mist be

free from scum, grease, hair scale dust, soil spillages and removable stains. In addition, the surfaces
should be disinfected.


Floors should be cleaned to the same standard as the building’s floors. In addition, there should be
no evidence of scum, grease, hair, and scale and the floors must be disinfected.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > E. Cleaning of all toilets :-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:

All Walls, skirting, dado-rails, coving, radiators, pipes, vents, grills, doors, doorframes, fittings and
glass panels, windows frames and sills must be free from debris, marks, and dust. They must be clean
and dry with no evidence of residual cleaning agents. In particular, they must be free from finger
marks, verdigris stains, runs and cobwebs to full height. Walls, doors and cubicle partitions shall be
washed by a disinfectant solution regularly.


Mirrors must be clean and free from smears.


Soap dispensers must be filled, operating correctly with clean nozzles the external surfaces must be
clean and replaces as necessary.


All toilets should be kept fully stocked with supplies and should be made available at all times.


Towel holders dispensers must be clean, dry and free from dust, marks an smears with clean towels
fitted. Hot air dryers must be clean, dry and free from dust, marks and smears.


Bins must be emptied cleaned and dried inside and out , bins liners replaced where necessary and
placed in their originals locations. Liners mist be used at all times.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > E. Cleaning of all toilets :-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres


The department expects a holistic washroom supplies service. The Vendor shall provide options on
the consolidation of existing and proposes washroom products.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > E. Cleaning of all toilets :-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

section_path: F. Walls, Ceilings, Doors and Staircase:-
text:
F. Walls, Ceilings, Doors and Staircase:-


All walls, skirting, dado-rails, coving, radiators, pipes, vents, grilles, doors, doorframes, fittings and
glass panels, window frames and sills must be free from debris, marks, and dust. They must be clean
and dry with no evidence of residual cleaning agents. In particular, they must be free from finger
marks, verdigris stains, runs, and cobwebs to full height.


All ceiling, ventilation diffusers and ceiling light fittings must be free from debris, marks, dust and
cobwebs. They must be dry with no evidence of residual cleaning agents.


Stairs including treads, risers, nosing, banisters, balustrades, handrails, ledges and protective wire
guards where present must be free from dust, debris, stains and marks.


Treads and risers are to be treated same as floors.


Walls and high-level surfaces and fitting must be free from dust, cobwebs and marks to the full
height.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > F. Walls, Ceilings, Doors and Staircase:-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
G. Corridors:-


All hard floor surfaces must be free from debris, clean, dry and from stains, marks and dust. There
must be no evidence of any accumulation of slurry of soaps or residues of other cleaning agents.
Floors must be safe and not slippery, some slight scuffing may be apparent, but the dressing must be
complete and intact without evidence of powdering, discoloration or build up.


All walls, skirting, dado-rails, coving, radiators, pipes vents, grilles, doors, doorframes, fittings and
glass panels, window frames and sills must be free from debris, marks and dust. They must be clean
free from finger marks verdigris stains, runs and cobwebs.


All carpets, mats and mat wells must be free from grit, dust and debris with no apparent stains. They
must be clean and dry.


Stainless steel surfaces must be treated with an appropriate cleaning and polishing agent.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > G. Corridors:-

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
H. External Areas: -


The Department requires the provision of a professionally managed cleaning service to the external
areas of the buildings.


The required service standard is to be evident before the start of activities and in addition should be
brought up to this standard during the business day.


Entrances, service areas, paving, paths, grounds and the outside premises must be maintained so
that no graffiti, debris, litter cigarette ends, dirt or spillages are apparent after cleaning. Empty all
waste bins and replace in their original locations.


All areas protected by security, screening, netting, protective cages etc. shall have the protection
removed temporarily to remove graffiti, debris, dirt dust, weeds and litter. The protection must be
replaced to the original standards prior to invasion.


The Bidder shall report any defects encountered during carrying out external area’s maintenance
tasks to the Department.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > H. External Areas: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
I. Periodic cleaning: -

In addition to the above the Bidder is required to carry out any periodic or deep clean activities not
included in the routine cleaning activities to achieve the service standards. This can include but is not
limited to deep cleaning and periodic cleaning activities of the communal and public areas and deep
cleaning activities that require more frequent cleaning than routine cleaning including kitchens,mess,
basement sump, basement drain and other areas as per the instruction of the Department.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > I. Periodic cleaning: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
J. Reactive Cleaning: -


A reactive service is required to maintain the full and safe use of the facilities. Tasks can include but
are not limited to responding to spillages, replenishing consumables, and monitoring the cleanliness
of the sanitary facilities.


Remove spills and treat to minimize damage to floor coverings and reduce the risk of staining. Use
only approved specialist materials within the indicated timescales for the removal and treatment of
spills.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 3 Scope ofwork > J. Reactive Cleaning: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
4. Safety Guidelines: -


The Bidder must know and follow their duties related to safety for all personnel. These guidelines are
applicable to Bidders as well as subbidders deployed by them at the site.


All Bidder workmen should be provided with a uniform by the Bidder and shall work within the
premises of the Group Centre in their prescribed uniform.


The Bidder shall ensure that no access (passages access to emergency apparatus exits) is blocked,
unless so authorized by Group Centre’s personnel beforehand.


The Bidder shall provide prior information to the Group Centre’s representative about any hazardous
material being brought on the site and shall ensure security storage of such material.


The Bidder must leave work areas in a clean, tidy, and safe condition at the end of each working
period.


The Bidder should ensure that their personnel do not chew tobacco,paan, gutkha, do not consume
alcohol, do not smoke, and do not take drugs on site.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 4. Safety Guidelines: -

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:

All workmen of the Bidder or their sub-bidders must have valid identifications cards verified by the
Group Centre’s administration& shall display at all times during duty hours.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 4. Safety Guidelines: -

9. Dispute Resolution

1. The bids and any contract resulting there from shall be governed by and construed according to the

Indian Laws.

2. All settlement of disputes or differences whatsoever, arising between the parties out of or in

connection to the construction, meaning and operation or effect of this Offer or in the discharge of
any obligation arising under this Offer (whether during the course of execution of the order or after
completion and whether before or after termination, abandonment or breach of the Agreement)
shall be resolved amicably between Department and the vendor’s representative.

3. In case of failure to resolve the disputes and differences amicably within 30 days of the receipt of

notice by the other party, then the same shall be resolved as follows:
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 9. Dispute Resolution

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
i. Conciliation: - All disputes or differences whatsoever arising between the parties out of or relating to
the construction, meaning, scope, operation or effect of this contract or the validity or the breach
thereof shall be first settled by way of conciliation and failing which, by way of arbitration in accordance
with the Rules of Arbitration of the Indian Council of Arbitration and the award made in pursuance
thereof shall be binding on the parties.
ii. The dispute shall be first referred to the Development Commissioner for conciliation who shall
conduct conciliationproceedings which will be held at Patna, Bihar.
iii. Arbitration: - In case the conciliation proceedings fail, the dispute shall be referred to the arbitration
as per the Arbitration Act.
iv. All legal disputes will come under the sole jurisdiction of Patna, Bihar. The venue of the arbitration
shall be Patna.

4. The Arbitral award shall be final and binding on both the parties.

5. Work under the contract shall be continued by the vendor during the arbitration proceedings unless
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 9. Dispute Resolution

be continued until the decision of the arbitrator is obtained. Save as those which are otherwise

10. Fraud or Corrupt Practices

1.
The Bidders shall observe the highest standard of ethics during the Bidding Process and

subsequent to the issue of the LOA and during the subsistence of the Agreement. Notwithstanding
anything to the contrary contained in this RFP, or in LOA or the Agreement, the DEPARTMENT may
reject a bid, withdraw the LOA, debar the bidder for a period of one year from participating in the
future projects of the Department or terminate the Agreement, as the case may be without being
liable in any manner whatsoever to the Bidder, if it determines that the Bidder has, directly or
indirectly or through an agent, engaged in corrupt practice, fraudulent practice, coercive practice,
undesirable practice or restrictive practices. In such an event, the DEPARTMENT shall, without
prejudice to its any other rights or remedies, forfeit and appropriate the Bid Security or Performance
Security as mutually agreed genuine pre- estimated compensation and damages payable to the

Authority for, inter alia, time, cost and effort of the Authority, in regard to the RFP, including
consideration and evaluation of such Bidders Proposal.
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 10. Fraud or Corrupt Practices

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
2.
Without prejudice to the rights of DEPARTMENT under Clause above and the rights and

remedies which the DEPARTMENT may have under the LOI or the Agreement, if a Bidder, is found by
the Authority to have directly or indirectly or through an agent, engaged or indulged in any corrupt
practice, fraudulent practice, coercive practice, undesirable practice or restrictive practice during the
Selection Process, or after the issue of the LOI or the execution of the Agreement, such Bidder shall
not be eligible to participate in any tender or RFP issued by DEPARTMENT during a period of
<1(one)year> from the date such Bidder, is found by DEPARTMENT to have directly or through an
agent, engaged or indulged in any corrupt practice, fraudulent practice, coercive practice,
undesirable practice or restrictive practice, as the case may be.

3.
For the purposes of this Section, the following terms shall have the meaning here in after

respectively assigned to them:

a) “corrupt practice” means the offering, giving, receiving or soliciting of anything of value, pressurizing to
context: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres > 10. Fraud or Corrupt Practices

metadata.title: RFP for Housekeeping Services at Group Centres

text:
influence the action of a public official in the process of tendering and execution of the project;

b) “fraudulent practice” means aim is representation or omission of facts or disclosure of incomplete

facts, in order to influence the Selection Process;

c) “coercive practice” means impairing or harming or threatening to impairer harm, directly or indirectly,

any persons or property to influence any person participation or action in the Selection Process;

d) “undesirable practice” means (i) establishing contact with any person connected with or employed or

engaged by Department with the objective of canvassing, lobbying or in any manner influencing or
attempting to influence the Selection Process; or (ii) having a Conflict of Interest; and

e) “restrictive practice” means forming a cartel or arriving at any understanding or arrangement among

Bidders with the objective of restricting or manipulating a full and fair competition in the Selection
process.

11. Termination & Blacklisting:

1. The Department may terminate this Agreement and Blacklist/Debar the vendor, in case of occurrence

of any of the events specified below. In the event of such an occurrence, the First Party may give not
less than 30 days written notice of termination to Second Party.

1. If the vendor is in material breach of its obligations pursuant to this Agreement and has not remedied

the same within 30 days.

2. If the vendor becomes insolvent or goes into compulsory liquidation

3. If the vendor, in the judgement of Department, has engaged in corrupt or fraudulent practices in

agreement by mutual consent in circumstances which does not constitute either party’s default without
any liability or consequential future liability for either party.

notice to the other Party and upon issuance of such notice, the other Party may within 15 days from

either of the two possible positions to the intending Party in writing.

section_path: SIGNATURE OF THE BIDDER WITH SEAL
text:
Note: -

1) The financial proposal shall include all costs associated with the scope of work. TheDepartmentshall not

bear any cost other than the total cost mentioned in the financial proposal.

2) Statutory Deduction, if applicable, shall be deducted at source from payment to the selected bidder as

per the law in force at the time of execution of the contract.

3) The agency will be required to provide approximately 60 staffs across the 3 Group Centres in 2 shifts

(morning/evening) as per the requirement of the Department.

4) All staffs should be well trained and must comply to the semi-skilled category.

5) The cost of all consumables etc as per scope of work will have to be provided by the agency at their own

cost and havetobuilt in the above quote.
